facts.raw_span: A man in his early 60s with pathologic myopia
had undergone multiple procedures, including vitrectomy and cataract surgery, on the left eye for a rhegmatogenous retinal detachment 2 years previously
had received multiple intravitreous ranibizumab injections to the left eye for myopic choroidal neovascularization
Best-corrected visual acuities were 20/40 OD and 20/200 OS
Revealed emulsified silicone oil forming a meniscus in the fovea of the left eye
Demonstrated the confinement of the hyperoleon within a lamellar macular hole
Color images of the left fundus
Spectral-domain optical coherence tomography (OCT) showing hyperreflective dots within a lamellar macular hole
En face swept source OCT showing oil bubbles within its boundaries

rationales.F01: The patient's age and pathologic myopia suggest a possible link to myopic choroidal neovascularization.
rationales.F02: The history of vitrectomy and cataract surgery for rhegmatogenous retinal detachment increases the likelihood of this condition.
rationales.F03: The use of intravitreous ranibizumab injections is a common treatment for myopic choroidal neovascularization.
rationales.F05: The presence of emulsified silicone oil in the fovea is a strong indicator of silicone oil-induced retinal toxicity and silicone oil retinopathy.
rationales.F06: The confinement of the hyperoleon within a lamellar macular hole is a characteristic feature of this condition.
rationales.F08: The presence of hyperreflective dots within a lamellar macular hole on OCT imaging supports the diagnosis of lamellar macular hole.
rationales.F09: The presence of oil bubbles within the boundaries of the lamellar macular hole on en face swept source OCT imaging is consistent with silicone oil retinopathy.
